articles.author: compilersutra
articles.description:
I wrote 6 lines of Triton…
and it turned into thousands of GPU instructions.
Python → TTIR → TTGIR → LLVM → AMDGCN → HSACO
👉 a + b → buffer_load_b128
👉 mask → v_cmp + conditional execution
Here’s the truth:
Your code is NOT what runs on the GPU.
The compiler builds an entire execution pipeline in between.
I dumped every stage and traced one kernel end-to-end 👇
https://www.compilersutra.com/docs/ml-compilers/mlcompilerstack/
After this, ML compilers don’t feel like “magic” anymore.
articles.title: AMD ML Complete Stack

Google Cloud's Metrics Explorer has plenty of metrics, and for most monitoring needs, it's more than enough.
However, the sampling interval of those metrics can hide real problems. I once ran into a situation where an API server on Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) had intermittent response time spikes, yet Metrics Explorer showed nothing abnormal. The root cause turned out to be short-lived batch jobs on the same Node eating up all the CPU, a classic Noisy Neighbor problem.
Here's how I fell into that trap.
I had a development API server running on GKE that would occasionally slow down for no obvious reason.
A request that normally completed in around 200 ms would sometimes take about 4 seconds, even under the same conditions. The slowdown was random/intermittent, and I could not find a clea…

articles.author: Nikola Brežnjak
articles.description:
TL;DR


I believe this book will improve your life immensely. It's one of those books where you have to get over your pride of "I don't need this", and then reap the benefits and wonder why no one told you this before. 😅
This book made it to my all time favorite list: If you want to improve, read these books.
I haven't posted a book post in a while, but this one absolutely deserves it.
I just finished The 5 Love Languages by Gary Chapman, and I honestly think it should be required reading for anyone. And, especially for those that are looking to get married. Call me weird, but I'd even suggest this as a hard requirement before the faithful YES.
Why am I so WOWed about it? Well, it's one of those "simple but powerful" books that can genuinely change how people understand each other. The core idea is incredibly practical: people give and receive love in different ways, and a lot of pain in relationships comes from missing that.
What makes the book so valuable is that it's immediately actionable. You don't just read it and nod along. You start noticing things. You start asking better questions. You start showing love in ways that actually land with your partner.
I truly believe this book could save a lot of marriages, relationships, and unnecessary heartbreak.
And no, it's not only for when you're already deep in trouble. It's great for when everything is perfectly fine - and after it, it gets even better.
If you're given this book, don't let your pride prevent you from reading it, and unlocking (IMHO) a superpower.
TL;DR: I highly recommend it.
Oh, and btw; just curious - if you read it, did it have the same/similar effect on you or am I just an outlier here?
articles.title: Book review: 5 Love Languages

articles.author: Munagala Karthik
articles.description:
Vibe coding is fun until it isn't.
You're flying through features. AI is writing everything. It feels like a superpower.
Then you hit the context limit.
The model forgets what it built. Starts contradicting itself. Code breaks in ways that make no sense. And suddenly you're spending more time fixing AI mistakes than you would have spent just writing it yourself.
I've been there.
The problem isn't vibe coding itself. The problem is depending on it completely.
If you don't understand what the code is doing you can't fix it when the AI loses the plot. And it will lose the plot.
Use it as a tool. Not a replacement for thinking.
Let AI handle the boilerplate. You handle the logic. You review every line. You stay in control.
The engineers who will win with AI are not the ones who prompt the best. They're the ones who know enough to catch when the AI is wrong.
Don't outsource your understanding. That's the one thing AI can't give back to you.


  
  
  DevOps #CloudSecurity
